chapter_seo_title: Chapter 391: The Mirror Fights Back – Li Huowang Faces a Zuowandao Who Stole His Powers
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang confronts a Zuowandao impostor in a haunted funeral hall—but this enemy has stolen his misalignment ability, his healing, and his skin. A desperate battle of identity theft begins.
og_description: The Zuowandao have infiltrated Apricot Island and stolen Li Huowang’s supernatural abilities. Now he must fight a perfect copy of himself with nothing left but raw desperation.
twitter_title: The Mirror Strikes: Li Huowang vs. a Zuowandao Who Stole His Moves
twitter_description: A Zuowandao impostor has stolen Li Huowang’s misalignment and healing powers. Can he survive a fight against a mirror that already knows every trick he has?

lore_anchors.definition: White lanterns hung at funeral processions or halls to guide the spirit of the deceased. The black character 奠 (diàn) marks the space as reserved for mourning rites.
Li Huowang’s signature spatial distortion trick, displacing his body within a one-zhang radius to avoid attacks. Having it stolen means the enemy can now use his own defensive technique against him.
A ritual weapon made of old Chinese coins strung together on red cord. Traditionally used in Daoist exorcism, it can also be deployed as a whip-like flexible blade.
The highest-ranked leaders of the Zuowandao sect. If this impostor is one of them, it explains his extraordinary ability to copy and steal supernatural powers.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang shout at the empty coffin?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is testing whether the funeral hall is haunted by a corpse or a spirit. If nothing attacks or responds, the threat is likely a false illusion or a living trickster.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How can a Zuowandao steal someone's supernatural ability?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the Dao-Twisted World, identities and abilities are not strictly bound to the body. A powerful illusionist or a high-ranking Zuowandao (like the Four Joys) can temporarily "borrow" or copy a target's innate powers by observing or mimicking their personal nature.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What happened to Li Huowang's fire ability?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He cannot self-immolate because his skin was already harvested and refined into a magical artifact. Without fresh skin to sacrifice, the ritual formula has no fuel to burn.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the teeth shrapnel attack?
cultural_notes_faq.a: His teeth cover a precise one-zhang radius—the exact range of his misalignment ability. By exploding his own teeth, he creates a complete kill zone that his stolen ability cannot escape.
